messages:
alex: FYI perf CI flagged a regression on release/v2026.03 — p95 latency up ~25% on gen workloads after merge abc123. Seen on two different machine types.
maria: ugh, which change? any stack traces or perf profiles?
alex: the merge touched kernel-selection heuristics + batching refactor. CI perf job: https://ci.redwood/ops/12345 — artifacts include flamegraphs. attaching quick snippet: 
```
p95_baseline: 120ms
p95_current: 150ms
hotspot: _select_kernels_for_batch (sched.cpp:214)
```
chen: I started a local repro on the staging GPU pool. Reproducer script: `tools/perf/run_client.py --model llama2-13b --seq 1024 --concurrency 8 --batching on`
sam: can you bisect to narrow the commit? we should confirm whether it's kernel-selection or batching.
alex: did a quick bisect: commit range def456..abc123. Narrowed to abc000 which introduced change to prefer fused kernel for short sequences. Removing that preference drops p95 back to baseline.
anya: if that's the case, we should not revert main yet — we need a release branch hotfix. Plan: revert on release branch, add test, then cherry-pick minimal fix to main.
maria: +1 on minimal patch. Also we need an isolated unit test to catch fused-kernel mis-selection for mixed-length batches.
chen: here's the temporary patch I tested locally (works):
```
--- a/runtime/scheduler/kernel_selector.cpp
+++ b/runtime/scheduler/kernel_selector.cpp
@@ -120,7 +120,9 @@
-    if (seq_len < FUSED_THRESHOLD) return FUSED_KERNEL;
+    // avoid selecting fused kernel when KV cache hit-rate < 0.6 in mixed batch
+    if (seq_len < FUSED_THRESHOLD && kv_cache_hitrate >= 0.6) return FUSED_KERNEL;
+    // otherwise fall back to generic kernel
```
sam: can you open a PR against release/v2026.03 with that change? tag it as hotfix and include perf CI link. I'll queue it for manual smoke on dedicated-dev infra.
alex: PR is up: https://git.redwood/r/release-hotfix/5678. CI run triggered (perf-suite-release).
ci-bot: perf-suite-release started for PR 5678 — job id 9876. Estimated finish ~12m.
maria: while CI runs, list of verification steps: 1) perf-suite passes 2) run small-scale smoke on dedicated-dev (sam) 3) run aKV trace to check KV-hit behavior (chen) 4) tag and backport to main if green
sam: running smoke now on dev-dedicated; reproducer run: `./tools/smoke.sh --pool dedicated-dev --runs 10`
ops-bot: dedicated-dev: all nodes healthy, capacity available.
chen: collecting KV traces, will check hit-rate distribution and kernel choice.
ci-bot: perf-suite-release finished — all checks OK. p95 regained to 122ms (within 2% of baseline). Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/ops/9876/artifacts
anya: good. next steps: cherry-pick the single-file patch to main, add unit test, and schedule a post-merge perf CI for main to validate. Who wants the cherry-pick?
sam: I'll handle cherry-pick to main and open follow-up PR with the test. Will also coordinate backport to any active release branches.
maria: please bump the changelog and add an entry to the rollout blockers doc so support knows why we reverted behavior.
alex: thanks everyone. I'll update the incident tracker with timeline and link to PRs/artifacts.
chen: one follow-up note: the fused kernel still gives benefits for pure short-seq workloads. We should add a telemetry guard (runtime flag) to enable/disable based on observed batch composition.
anya: agreed — adding to roadmap for batching heuristics work. For now hotfix shipped. :tada:
